data.text:
Over the past decade, remote work has moved from a rare perk to a mainstream arrangement for many office staff. In my view, working from home offers very good things to both workers and companies, although it is not without drawbacks.

For employees, the most obvious advantage is the time saved on commuting. In a city such as Dhaka, where a single journey can take more than an hour, people who works from home can spend this time with their kids or get some rest before starting work. This tends to improve concentration during working hours. Also, workers are happier. Also they stay longer in the same company.

In the other hand, employers benefit from lower office costs, which mean they can invest more in staff training. A company that no longer rents a big office in the city centre can save a lot of money every year. Moreover, managers can hire talented staff from other cities, which widens the pool of applicants.

Admittedly, some workers feel lonely at home, and it is really difficult for new staff to learn from their colleagues. For instance, a junior accountant may not know who to ask when a question appears. However, regular video meetings and one office day per week can solve most of these difficulties.

In conclusion, I believe that working from home benefits both employees and employers. If companies organise it carefully, the advantages are much greater than the disadvantages, and both sides will be more productive and more satisfied in the long term.
data.prompt: Some people believe that working from home benefits both employees and employers. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
feedback: Use more precise vocabulary instead of informal words.

data.text:
The bar chart compares the value of coffee exports from Brazil, Vietnam, Colombia and Ethiopia in 2010 and 2020.

Overall, Brazil was by far the largest exporter in both years, although its exports fell slightly over the decade. The other three countries saw small increases.

In 2010, Brazil exported coffee worth 5.7 billion dollars, which was three times more than Vietnam and Colombia, which both earned 1.9 billion. Ethiopia had the lowest value at only 0.8 billion. By 2020, the figure for Brazil went down to 4.9 billion.

Colombia had the biggest rise, and its exports reached 2.5 billion dollars. Vietnam also increase to 2.2 billion. But Ethiopia stayed almost the same, with a small change from 0.8 to 0.9 billion dollars.

To sum up, Brazil remained the leader, but the gap between it and the other countries got smaller over the period.

feedback: Group similar countries together to make comparisons clearer.
Use a wider range of verbs to describe change (declined, climbed, levelled off).

data.text:
Traffic congestion is a serious problem in many cities around the world. Some people argue that governments should invest in public transport, while others believe that building more roads is the best solution. This essay will discuss both views before giving my opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of new roads say that wider streets allow cars to move faster. In countries where many people already own a car, more roads can reduce journey times in the short term. In addition, roads are essential for delivery trucks, which carry food and other goods to shops.

On the other hand, I think that spending on buses and trains is a better long-term plan. A single train can carry a lot of passengers, so it takes hundreds of cars off the road. Moreover, public transport produces less pollution per person, which is important for the health of people who live in big cities. Studies also show that new roads often fill up with more cars within a few years, so the problem soon returns.

And public transport helps poorer people who cannot afford a car to reach jobs and schools. This makes society more fair and it's good for the economy.

In conclusion, although building roads can give quick relief, I believe governments should spend more money on public transport because it is cheaper, cleaner and fairer in the long run.
data.prompt: Some people think governments should spend more money on public transport, while others believe building more roads is the better way to reduce traffic. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
feedback: Give one specific example to support the road-building view.
Check comparative forms and avoid contractions.

data.text:
The diagram show how water moves around the Earth in a cycle.

First, the sun heats the water in the oceans and it turns into water vapour. This vapour goes up into the sky. When it is high, the air is cold so the vapour becomes small drops of water and makes clouds.

Next, the clouds move over the land with the wind. When the drops get heavy, they fall down as rain or snow. This is called precipitation. Some of the rain runs over the ground into rivers and lakes, and some goes into the soil and becomes groundwater.

Finally the water in rivers and under the ground goes back to the sea. Then the sun heats it again and the whole process starts again from the beginning.

In conclusion, the water cycle has four main stages which are evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection, and it never stops.
data.prompt: The diagram shows the water cycle, the continuous movement of water on, above and below the surface of the Earth. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
feedback: Begin with an overview of the number of stages in the process.
Use the passive voice to describe processes (water is heated…).

Nowadays many people work from home instead of going to the office. I think this is good for workers and also for companies, but there are some problems too.

Firstly, workers do not need to travel, so they save a lot of time and money. In Dhaka the traffic is very heavy and people spend two hours every day on the bus. If they work at home they can sleep more and they are not tired.

Secondly, companies can pay less for offices. They don't need a big building so they can use the money for other things like salaries. Also the workers are more happy so they do not leave the company.

But there are some disadvantages. Some people feel alone at home and they cannot ask their colleagues when they have a problem. Also the internet is sometimes slow in some areas.

In conclusion, I think working from home is good for both workers and companies, but the companies should help the workers who feel alone.
